introduction.p: Determine the domain of each of the following functions. In each case, write a sentence to accurately describe the domain.

answer.p: The domain of f is all real numbers.

solution.p: The denominator x^2+1 is always positive, so it is never zero. The domain of f is all real numbers.

answer.p: The domain of g is all real numbers except x = 1 and x = -4.

solution.p: Factoring the denominator: x^2+3x-4 = (x-1)(x+4). The denominator is zero when x = 1 or x = -4. The domain of g is all real numbers except x = 1 and x = -4.

answer.p: The domain of h is all real numbers except x = 0, x = 1, and x = 2.

solution.p: Each fraction is undefined when its denominator is zero: 1/x is undefined at x=0, 1/(x-1) is undefined at x=1, and 1/(x-2) is undefined at x=2. The domain of h is all real numbers except x = 0, x = 1, and x = 2.

answer.p: The domain of j is all real numbers except x = -1, x = -3, and x = 5.

solution.p: The denominator is zero when x = -1, x = -3, or x = 5. The domain of j is all real numbers except x = -1, x = -3, and x = 5.

answer.p: The domain of k is all real numbers except x = -2, x = 0, and x = 2.

solution.p: Factoring the denominator: 3x^3 - 12x = 3x(x^2 - 4) = 3x(x-2)(x+2). The denominator is zero when x = 0, x = 2, or x = -2. The domain of k is all real numbers except x = -2, x = 0, and x = 2.

answer.p: The domain of m is all real numbers except x = -1, x = 2, and x = 3.

solution.p: The denominator is zero when x = 2, x = 3, or x = -1 (the factor x^2+9 has no real zeros since x^2 \geq 0). The domain of m is all real numbers except x = -1, x = 2, and x = 3.
